source_reference_read: Semanario del Nuevo Reyno de Granada año 2 núm. 5 (5 Feb 1809), Banco de la República Biblioteca Virtual p17054coll26 id 1606 (PDF downloaded 16 Oct 2026; also hosted at sources/scans/semanario_nrg_1809_no05_banrep1606/): masthead p. 33, Noticia meteorológica pp. 37-40 and the NOTA on p. 40
notes: William read every cited page from the image in his own modernised-spelling transcription. Masthead: Núm. 5, Santafé 5 de Febrero de 1809. Start date printed in words, 'once de Diciembre'. Silver sun mistaken for the Moon, no coronas, 4th-5th magnitude stars gone, veil constant day and night, Pasto/Popayán/Neiva/Santa Marta/Tunja all present. NOTA: 'el fenómeno que ha dos meses observamos'. Claude listed what to look for but did not read the pages for him. Item rights: Dominio público (U181).

source_reference_read: Semanario del Nuevo Reyno de Granada 1808, JCB copy archive.org semanariodelnuev01unse (PDF on William's Mac): núm. 7 masthead (PDF p. 73, printed p. 51); code key and 'velo' footnote 3 (PDF p. 78, printed p. 56); monthly tables Jan-Jul 1808 (PDF pp. 71, 105 [Feb, núm. 10, printed p. 83], 131, 165, 199, 245, 281)
notes: Confirms the finding as corrected; the earlier AI record had three errors. (1) Corona entry 'S ve. cla. cor. S.' was dated 14 Feb; William read day 14 as 'C. cal. nieb.'; the sky column is printed half a row high; counting entries from top and bottom puts it on 15 Feb. (2) The Feb table is in núm. 10 (6 Mar 1808), not núm. 7. (3) Veils were said to occur 'a handful of times a month'; William's check of every month gives ve. on 10 of 212 days (Feb 9, 15, 29; Mar 4, 12, 20, 23; Apr 4; May 6 printed 've. sep.'; Jun 28 'vel.'; none Jan, Jul), corona with veil 15 Feb (Sun) and 12 Mar (Moon), lunar corona without veil 3 Apr. June has 29 sky entries for 30 days; William reads line 1 as blank (day 1 thermometers 00,0), so 28 Jun; Claude first counted 27 Jun. See CHECKS_README, Corrections caught by human checks, no. 1.
